# agenco_conditional_policy (Resource)

Manages a conditional access policy — an if/then rule deciding whether a tool call is allowed, denied, stepped up or sent for approval.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Refunds outside the EU need an approval flow; everything else is allowed.
resource "agenco_conditional_policy" "refund_approval" {
  name    = "Refunds need approval outside the EU"
  enabled = true

  application_ids   = [agenco_application.storefront.id]
  internal_tool_ids = [agenco_tool.refund.id]

  targeting {
    if {
      condition_logic = "and"

      condition {
        attribute = "country"
        op        = "in_list"
        negate    = true
        value     = jsonencode({ list = ["DE", "FR", "NL", "IE"] })
      }
    }

    then {
      result           = "approval_required"
      approval_flow_id = var.refund_approval_flow_id
    }
  }
}

# Nested groups express "(A and B) or C".
resource "agenco_conditional_policy" "step_up_risky" {
  name    = "Step up risky sessions"
  enabled = true

  application_ids   = [agenco_application.storefront.id]
  internal_tool_ids = []

  targeting {
    if {
      condition_logic = "or"

      condition_group {
        condition_logic = "and"

        condition {
          attribute = "user-agent"
          op        = "contains"
          negate    = false
          value     = jsonencode({ list = ["curl"] })
        }

        condition {
          attribute = "tool-name"
          op        = "starts_with"
          negate    = false
          value     = jsonencode({ list = ["delete"] })
        }
      }

      condition {
        attribute = "country"
        op        = "in_list"
        negate    = false
        value     = jsonencode({ list = ["RU", "KP"] })
      }
    }

    then {
      result               = "step_up"
      step_up_action_async = true
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the policy is evaluated. A disabled policy may omit targeting.
- `internal_tool_ids` (Set of String) Internal tool IDs the policy applies to. Pass an empty set to apply to all tools.
- `name` (String) Policy name.

### Optional

- `allow_to_all_users` (Boolean) Whether the policy result applies to all users.
- `application_ids` (Set of String) Applications the policy applies to. Omit to apply across the vendor.
- `custom_code_tool_ids` (Set of String) Custom code tool IDs the policy applies to.
- `custom_integration_tools` (Set of String) Connector tool API IDs the policy applies to, formatted {integration_id}_{group}_{action}, for example slack_chat_postMessage.
- `description` (String) Free-text description of what the policy does.
- `metadata` (Map of String) Free-form string metadata stored alongside the policy.
- `slug` (String) Restrict the policy to one connector instance by slug. Omit to cover every instance.
- `targeting` (Block List) Targeting rule deciding when the policy applies and what it does. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--targeting))
- `tenant_id` (String) Restrict the policy to a single tenant. Omit for a vendor-level policy.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Policy ID.

<a id="nestedblock--targeting"></a>
### Nested Schema for `targeting`

Optional:

- `if` (Block List) Conditions that must match. Omit to apply the policy unconditionally. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--targeting--if))
- `then` (Block List) The outcome applied when the conditions match. Exactly one is required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--targeting--then))

<a id="nestedblock--targeting--if"></a>
### Nested Schema for `targeting.if`

Optional:

- `condition` (Block List) A condition evaluated against the request. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--targeting--if--condition))
- `condition_group` (Block List) A nested group of conditions with its own logic operator. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--targeting--if--condition_group))
- `condition_logic` (String) How the top-level conditions and groups combine. One of: and, or. The API defaults it to and when omitted.

<a id="nestedblock--targeting--if--condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `targeting.if.condition`

Required:

- `attribute` (String) Request attribute to evaluate, for example ip, country, roles or tool-name.
- `negate` (Boolean) Whether to invert the comparison result.
- `op` (String) Comparison operator, for example in_list, equal, matches or between_numeric.
- `value` (String) Comparison operand as a JSON object string. Its shape follows op, for example {"list":["US"]} for in_list or {"number":5} for equal.


<a id="nestedblock--targeting--if--condition_group"></a>
### Nested Schema for `targeting.if.condition_group`

Required:

- `condition_logic` (String) How the conditions in this group combine. One of: and, or.

Optional:

- `condition` (Block List) A condition evaluated against the request. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--targeting--if--condition_group--condition))

<a id="nestedblock--targeting--if--condition_group--condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `targeting.if.condition_group.condition`

Required:

- `attribute` (String) Request attribute to evaluate, for example ip, country, roles or tool-name.
- `negate` (Boolean) Whether to invert the comparison result.
- `op` (String) Comparison operator, for example in_list, equal, matches or between_numeric.
- `value` (String) Comparison operand as a JSON object string. Its shape follows op, for example {"list":["US"]} for in_list or {"number":5} for equal.




<a id="nestedblock--targeting--then"></a>
### Nested Schema for `targeting.then`

Required:

- `result` (String) Policy outcome. One of: [allow deny step_up approval_required mask].

Optional:

- `approval_flow_id` (String) Approval flow to run. Required when result is approval_required.
- `step_up_action_async` (Boolean) Whether a step_up result is triggered asynchronously rather than requiring the user to retry. Only meaningful when result is step_up.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import agenco_conditional_policy.refund_approval 66667777-8888-9999-0000-111122223333
```
